# European AI Labour Market Synthesis — What Survives the Stress Test
> https://synthesis.nexalps.com/

## What this is
Part 6 of 7 in the Nexalps European AI Labour Market suite. A corridor map across all 36 European labour markets — EU-27 plus EFTA, the United Kingdom, and four candidate countries — scored across five lenses, stress-tested under eight scenarios, bracketed into four fragility classes.

## Author + publication
Philipp Maul, Nexalps (https://nexalps.com). Published April 2026.

## Headline finding
Of 36 European labour markets, only 9 remain conditionally resilient under stress: Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Iceland, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden. Under the strict-zero rule applied to the corrected thresholds (1.20 / 2.80), zero countries qualify — even Norway and Sweden fail strict robustness. There is no unconditionally safe European labour market at the corrected threshold.

## Key findings
1. Strict-zero Class I — published "managed transition" base rates over-state robustness. Under the strict (b) ±0 rule applied to corrected thresholds (1.20 / 2.80), Class I count drops to 0.
2. Demographic ageing does not absorb displacement. Maximum retirement-offset reading across 32 scored countries is ~26% against the 80% buffer threshold; zero countries clear. Italy is the standout demographic case: 2025 net migration −485,823.
3. The optimism path narrows to Climate Zone-C. Three countries (Austria, Luxembourg, Türkiye) reach C1 only under S2 Climate Adaptation Boom; all other routine variants land them in C2 or C3.
4. Averages hide a split in the high-coordination cluster. At 2-digit ISCO, teaching-heavy weight (0.582) is 3.7× ICT weight (0.157). Education / admin lift (DK, IS, LU, NO) versus finance / tech drag (CH, DE, IE, UK).
5. The squeeze cluster is eight worker-protection economies, two distinct mechanisms. Nordic sub-cluster (DK, FI, NO, SE): worker-protection × trade-decoupling. Continental sub-cluster (BE, DE, FR, NL): worker-protection × UK adjacency × Mode 1 capital-flow vulnerability.
6. Pan-European aggregate. No single European corridor — the centre of gravity sits in C2 + C3, with 9 markets resilient, 9 fragile, 15 already in trouble, and 3 in currently failing. Within the EU-27 specifically: 7 / 6 / 14 / 0 across Class I / II / III / IV.
7. Reskilling capacity gap. Across EU-27 + UK: deep-reskilling cohort by 2035 ~7.55 M; ~450 K net new annual transition capacity; 15-year backlog; 5–9-year speed gap between AI disruption (1–3 years) and reskilling-system response.
8. Capability-floor breach. 12 countries fall below the institutional adaptive-capacity floor at the 2-digit ESCO-weighted ceiling.

## Eight scenarios (seven routine + one conditional)
- S1 Reinstatement Revival — uber-optimistic. Historical base rate is biased upward (Autor 2024 reinstatement-effect weakening); bounded above. Under post-growth, requires expanding output, weaker.
- S2 Climate Adaptation Boom (Zone-C) — optimistic. Cedefop 2025 + EU Net-Zero Industry Act €100 B clean-manufacturing envelope; the only routine path to C1 for AT, LU, TR.
- S3 Jobs Transform — slightly optimistic. AI substitutes for routine sub-tasks within existing occupations; reinstatement effect operates within-occupation. Anchored on Brynjolfsson 2025 (OpenAI productivity RCT), Dell'Acqua 2024 (BCG consultants), historical ATM/teller and spreadsheet analogues.
- S4 Muddle Through — middle baseline. Mixed reinstatement and absorption; partial-coverage outcome.
- S5 Wage Cliff — slightly pessimistic. Mid-skill wage compression with absorption gap; substitution-dominated dynamics.
- S6 Reinstatement Failure — pessimistic. Autor 2024 weakening of new-work creation; primary anchor for the corrected corridor edges.
- S7 Bandwidth Fracture — pessimistic. Institutional bandwidth tax from defence + climate + migration commitments crowds out ALMP capacity.
- S8 Polycrisis Drag — parallel cascade, conditional, orthogonal to S1–S7. Compounding climate × geopolitics × fiscal stress; carried as conditional.

## Three corridors
- C1 Managed Transition (ratio < 1.20). 5 countries: DK, FI, IS, NO, SE. Displacement velocity well-absorbed by ALMP capacity.
- C2 Partial Absorption (1.20–2.80). 16 countries. ALMP partially absorbs displacement; sectoral and regional reabsorption uneven.
- C3 Displacement Without Absorption (≥ 2.80). 15 countries. ALMP capacity insufficient; lifetime-earnings deficits expected (El-Sahli & Upward 2017).

## Four fragility classes
- Class I — Robust (relative-stable, C3-guarded). 9 countries: BE, DK, FI, FR, IS, LU, NL, NO, SE.
- Class II — Fragile. 9 countries: AT, BA, BG, CH, DE, ES, LI, LV, RO. Baseline stable but at least one routine variant lands C3.
- Class III — Pre-Failure Risk. 15 countries: CY, CZ, EE, EL, HR, HU, IE, IT, LT, MT, PL, PT, SI, SK, UK. S4 Muddle Through baseline lands in C3 post-rescaling.
- Class IV — Currently Failing. 3 countries: MK, RS, TR. Candidate-partial-coverage with extreme Lens 5 readings.

## Three economic regimes
- growth-baseline — 24 markets.
- secular-stagnation-warning — 2 markets: Greece, Italy.
- post-growth-empirical — 10 markets: AT, CH, DE, FI, FR, LI, LU, NO, SE, UK.

## Reskilling capacity anchor
Across EU-27 + UK: deep-reskilling cohort by 2035 ~7.55 M; gross high-exposure ~38.72 M; annual throughput ~3.34 M of which ~2.89 M is consumed by baseline economic churn (Eurostat lfsa_etpgan tenure-under-1yr proxy), leaving ~450 K net new annual transition capacity. Implied backlog: 15 years. Speed gap between AI disruption (1–3 years) and reskilling-system response (5–9 years).

## Class distributions
- 36-market scope: Class I / II / III / IV = 9 / 9 / 15 / 3.
- EU-27 only: Class I / II / III / IV = 7 / 6 / 14 / 0.
